content:
The product of two numbers is a perfect square exactly when they have the same square-free kernel.

So all marked numbers must have the same square-free part \(k\).  
For a fixed square-free \(k\), the marked numbers are of the form \(k m^2 \le 2016\), so there are

\[
\left\lfloor \sqrt{\frac{2016}{k}} \right\rfloor
\]

such numbers.

This is maximized when \(k=1\), giving the perfect squares:

\[
1^2,2^2,\dots,44^2
\]

since \(44^2=1936\le 2016<45^2=2025\).

\[
\boxed{44}
\]
